successors.name: House of Jagiellon
successors.text: Poland and Lithuania under one ruler, Cliopatria's Jagiellonian row from 1450

ledger.x: c. 960: Mieszko I rules the Polans from Gniezno. Infobox 'c. 960-992', the polity 'centered around Gniezno' with its 'capital in Gniezno'; Mieszko is the 'ruler of the Polans' who accepted Christianity in 966 (Baptism of Poland), bishopric at Poznań 968. The page gives no boundary; Cliopatria's first shape (962) is…

c. 980: Pomerania, the Baltic coast and the first of Lesser Poland join. The page is silent on the date: of Mieszko I it says only that Pomerania, Silesia, Lesser Poland and Lubusz 'are not mentioned'; the Dagome iudex (c. 991-992) is quoted as running from 'the long sea' (the Baltic), naming Kraków…
990: Mieszko I takes Silesia and Lesser Poland from Bohemia.
1002: Bolesław invades Lusatia and Meissen.
July 1002: Henry II confirms Bolesław in Lusatia.

c. 1003: Moravia comes under Bolesław. 'It is also likely that Polish forces took control of Moravia and the northern parts of the Kingdom of Hungary'; the page dates the conquest '1003 or 1015' and says the area 'stayed a part of Poland until 1018'. The page does not say who held Moravia; the Bohemian duchy is the…
c. 1003: the north of the Kingdom of Hungary (Slovakia) comes under Bolesław ('the northern parts of the Kingdom of Hungary'; '1003 or 1015').
March 1003: Bolesław is proclaimed duke of Bohemia in Prague.
8 September 1004: Bohemia is lost.
1005: Lusatia and Meissen are lost at the peace of Poznań.
1005: a pagan rising takes Pomerania out of Polish hands.
1007: Bolesław re-occupies the Lusatian marches.
1018: Moravia is given up.
1018: the north of Hungary (Slovakia) is given up; the same 'until 1018' sentence.
30 January 1018: the Peace of Bautzen ends the German war.
30 January 1018: Bautzen leaves the Lusatian marches Polish soil, no longer imperial fiefs: 'not as fiefs, but as a part of Polish territory'.
August 1018: Bolesław takes Kiev and re-annexes the Red Strongholds.
1025: Bolesław I crowns himself king of Poland (generally assumed Easter, 27 March 1025; Wojciechowski argues 24 December 1024).
1031: Mieszko II loses the crown and the kingdom shrinks to a duchy again.

c. 1031: Conrad II regains Lusatia. 'Conrad II's forces attacked Poland and regained Lusatia.' The page gives no year; 1031 is the year of the crown's loss on the Kingdom page. Cliopatria drops the German part by 1034.

c. 1031-1034: the Red Strongholds fall away again. The Casimir I page is silent on Cherven/Red Ruthenia; the Kingdom page says only 'territorial losses' after 1031. Cliopatria's 1034 shape no longer holds the Lublin and Subcarpathian lands.
1034-1039: the realm contracts to its core.
c. 1038: the capital leaves Gniezno for Kraków. Kingdom page infobox: 'Gniezno (until 1038), Kraków (until 1793)'; the Casimir page says 'the capital of Poland was moved to Kraków' without a date.
1039: Bretislaus I of Bohemia invades.
1040: Casimir I the Restorer retakes most of the realm.
1047: Casimir subdues Masovia.
1050: Casimir seizes Silesia back from Bohemia.
1076: Bolesław II regains the crown and Poland is a kingdom again; page: '1076-1079: Bolesław II regains the crown, then is excommunicated and banished'.
1079: Bolesław II is excommunicated and banished; Poland is a duchy again.
1115: Bolesław III invades Gdańsk Pomerania.
1119: the conquest of Gdańsk Pomerania is complete ('from 1115 to 1119').
1119: Gdańsk Pomerania passes to Poland.
1121: Bolesław marches on Szczecin.
1122: Western Pomerania submits.
1122: Western Pomerania becomes a Polish fief ('which became a Polish fief'); Wolin and Usedom are taken in 1128-1129 and Rügen is raided in 1130 with Danish support.
1138: the Pomeranian fief is listed as its own division.
28 October 1138: Bolesław III dies and divides Poland among his sons.
1138: Masovia becomes a duchy of its own, one of the six divisions the Kingdom page names.
1138: Silesia becomes a duchy of its own, one of the six divisions the Kingdom page names.
1138: Sandomierz becomes a duchy of its own, one of the six divisions the Kingdom page names.
26 June 1295: Przemysł II is crowned King of Poland at Gniezno, the first attempt to restore the kingdom.
1305: Władysław the Elbow-high masters Sandomierz.
1305: Brześć Kujawski and Sieradz-Łęczyca come to Władysław; Wenceslaus II, 'the Czech and Polish king', died this year.
1 September 1306: Władysław enters Kraków.
End of 1306: Pomerania is made subordinate.
13 November 1308: Polish suzerainty over Pomerelia ends.
13 November 1308: Poland and the Teutonic Order contest Pomerelia.
1314: Władysław conquers all of Greater Poland.
January 1320: Władysław I is crowned in Kraków and the kingdom is restored.
1329: the Teutonic Order begins the conquest of Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land.
1332: the conquest is complete and the land is held, not fought over, until the 1343 peace ('between 1329 and 1332').
1332: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land pass to the Teutonic Order, 'conquered by the Teutonic Order between 1329 and 1332'.
November 1335: the Visegrád arbitration.
June 1340: Casimir III takes Lviv.

8 July 1343: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land return to Poland by the Treaty of Kalisz ('King Casimir III regained Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land'); Casimir 'undertook to raise no future claims on Pomerelia, as well as Chełmno Land and Michałów Land'.
1344: Poland and Lithuania make peace over Galicia-Volhynia: 'Volhynia was assigned to Liubartas and Galicia to Casimir'.
1344: Galicia (Red Ruthenia) goes to Casimir III ('Galicia to Casimir').
1348: Volhynia becomes the object of the Polish-Hungarian-Lithuanian war.
1352: Masovia enters the Polish shape.
Autumn 1366: Casimir III beats Liubartas.
Autumn 1366: western Volhynia passes to Casimir III's allies.
ledger.cp: Yuri and Aleksander, sons of Karijotas

ledger.x: 1370: Liubartas retakes western Volhynia.
ledger.cp: Yuri and Aleksander, sons of Karijotas

ledger.x: 5 November 1370: Casimir III dies and the Piast line ends; Louis I of Hungary of the House of Anjou 'became king in 1370'.
1378: Louis attaches Galicia directly to Hungary.
4 March 1386: Jogaila is crowned Władysław II Jagiełło, the Jagiellon dynasty begins after the Union of Krewo (1385) and his marriage to Queen Jadwiga.
1387: Galicia returns to Poland for good.
25 June 1431: Poland invades Volhynia.
15 October 1432: the Union of Grodno.
15 October 1432: Podolia and part of Volhynia pass to Poland by the Union of Grodno.
1449: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends and its House of Jagiellon row (Poland with Lithuania in one union) begins in 1450.

wars.name: German-Polish War of 1002-1018 (Lusatia, Meissen, Bohemia)
wars.outcome: Peace of Bautzen, 30 January 1018: Bolesław kept the Lusatian marches 'not as fiefs, but as a part of Polish territory'.

wars.name: Kiev expedition of 1018
wars.outcome: Bolesław captured Kiev (it 'surrendered upon seeing the main Polish force on 14 August'), installed his son-in-law Sviatopolk I, and re-annexed the Red Strongholds, 'later called Red Ruthenia'.

wars.name: Bohemian invasion of 1039 and Casimir's restoration
wars.outcome: Bretislaus I sacked Gniezno and took part of Silesia with Wrocław in 1039; Casimir I returned with German and Kievan support in 1039-1040, seized Silesia in 1050 and at Quedlinburg in 1054 the Emperor left it to Poland for a yearly tribute of 117 kg of silver…

wars.name: Casimir I's war against Masovia
wars.outcome: 'In 1047, Casimir started a war against Masovia and seized the land.'

wars.name: Bolesław III's conquest of Pomerania
wars.outcome: Gdańsk Pomerania conquered 1115-1119, Szczecin 1121-1122, Western Pomerania made a Polish fief in 1122, Wolin and Usedom taken with Danish troops in 1128-1129, an expedition to Rügen in 1130; the Merseburg congress of 1135 addressed Pomerania.

wars.name: Bolesław III's wars with Bohemia and Hungary
wars.outcome: Svatopluk made duke of Bohemia on 14 May 1107; Hundsfeld, 24 August 1109 (historians doubt it); 'a decisive victory against the Czechs at the Battle of Trutina on 8 October 1110'; a Bohemian-Hungarian-Rus coalition 'achieved complete victory over the Polish…

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332)
wars.outcome: 'A Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332) occupied Władysław's last years'; Płowce, Kuyavia, 27 September 1331.

wars.name: Galicia-Volhynia Wars
wars.outcome: Lviv taken June 1340; 1344 peace 'Volhynia was assigned to Liubartas and Galicia to Casimir'; 1348 Liubartas loses land except eastern Volhynia with Lutsk; 1352 truce 'rather favourable to the Lithuanians'; 1366 Liubartas beaten and left only eastern Volhynia…

wars.name: Polish intervention in the Lithuanian Civil War (1431-1432)
wars.outcome: Polish army invaded Volhynia on 25 June 1431 and took part of Volhynia, Horodło, Volodymyr-Volynskyi and Zbarazh; the Teutonic Knights were beaten at Dąbki on 13 September 1431; truce of 1 September 1431 'more favorable to Poland'; Union of Grodno, 15 October…

certainty.note: Piast frontiers on the Oder, the Baltic, the Carpathians and the Bohemian and Rus' marches are approximate.
No Cliopatria shape: the land is the duchies' (their own dossiers).
The Teutonic frontier (Visegrád 1335) and the Galician-Volhynian line (1392 Ostrów Agreement) are treaty lines the pages name but do not draw; Podolia and Volhynia stay soft.
